The world has forgotten that all things must end, and in so doing caused destruction among themselves to achieve eternalism. Death comes for all of us. Don’t you understand this? Even Gods. Even Immortals. These are all under the inevitable executioner’s blade of Daklaon, Great Time, who has manifested upon this very world as the Unconquerable Charnel Maiden.

The Unconquerable Maiden is the tutelary deity of charnel grounds, cemeteries, crypts, mausoleums, and all places of death. Of accidents, of executions, of genocides, of suicides. She is there, always kind, always understanding. Then, with her Subatomic Blade, she flenses away the Phenomenal VIO, and tosses you into the Interstitial. The Unconquerable Maiden is Death. And none can conquer Death.

In Infinite and Mystic Law, the Unconquerable Maiden is an incarnation of Kroma Nagmi, the Enlightened One of Killing.

Truth · d66 [5][3]

The state faith of the Amatsunese Empire. A consolidation of a thousand thousand indigenous rituals and god-worships, as well as ancestor reverences. The world has fallen into disarray because the deities have been ignored. This is a spirit world! To forget them, to not do their rituals, is to invite annihilation.

The Fires will only be kept back by the Gods. Ritual and worship of the various deities and spirits that own this world. Create Heavenly Gates, Sacred Towers, and Spirit Shrines to appease them. Many priests and shamans follow this. It is because of them that the spirits are appeased. It is the ancestors that know the future, that know the past, and that know the inner workings of the world violent.

Follow the ways of the Ancestors. Remember everything that now exists is passed down by the Ancestors, by those that have come before us. Humble yourself. You are in the presence of a thousand watching eyes. They can change your fate in a minute.

Truth · d66 [5][4]

All three things cast aloft: Heaven begets Earth begets Man begets Heaven. The reality of the world is in the Supreme Principle of the Three-As-One. Ya, Earth. Ji, Heaven. And Yaji, Man.

There are no words to describe the Yaji. And so I will describe everything else, so that the emptiness may be its shape. It is the held breath. The spine’s truth as you bend down to the soil, the rightness in the stone’s grain. After the war, we tried to build a world from it. We made it seeing stone for the collective. For the masses. Led by the great Masangwa.

To practice is to listen for the alignment. The blacksmith who forgets his hands is Yaji. The river wearing the stone smooth is Yaji. We move as inquiry: through the meridians of our own flesh, through the silence that fills the mouth after a chant, through the herbal steam from the alchemist’s cup. Inscribe talismans as to beg for fortune and fate. Worship ancestors to remind ourselves of our mortal existence.

To experience the Yaji is, in essence, to live in harmony with nature, for nature is the ultimate, most primeval expression of the Yaji. To live in harmony with nature is to live in harmony with Heaven and Earth.

Truth · d66 [5][5]

Rationalists believe reason, that which we use to make sense of the world that we perceive, is the chief source of true knowledge. Due to new developments in sciences, Rationalists have taken an upsurge once again, believing that the world we have can only be truly perceived through our senses and therefore is only real through our reason and rationality.

They therefore believe that we must take the reins of humanity ourselves and create knowledge that we know will be beneficial to us. Most Rationalists espouse belief in a higher power, spiritual power, or other powers that we cannot inherently understand, as those are not real to them.

Additionally, Rationalists tend to be innately fiercely libertarian, putting above all else the Reasoning-Being’s faculties, personhood, and autonomy above all else.

Truth · d66 [5][6]

An occult application of Masangwaist Class Analysis, applied to the Gods. The belief that the Gods in Heaven and Earth are metaphysical aristocrats that must be overthrown by the Ruled Realms--the humans, the demons, the spirits, and the hungry ghosts.

Headed by Shaman-Magister Wo Sa Tien of the Demon Maw Sect, Demonism seeks to make allies with beings of negative karma and evil sorceries to toss down Heaven and free the people once and for all, in turn Breaking The Wheel.

Wo Sa Tien is sometimes revered as an emanation of Jizosatsu Martyr-Savior, the Lord of Six Ways, while others--especially South Shennins and Demonkind, revere him as Wongo Enlightened One, the Buddha of Emancipatory Emptiness.

Truth · d66 [6][1]

Beyond materialism. Ultramaterialism arose during the Decades of Carnage where materialism ran its course in the scholarly circles of Jeng, the Charnel Isles, and the Heavenshards. Following a long line of Munian Existentialists and Rationalists, starting from Kunzt and ending, inevitably, with Frunstenst Haggia of Mun Idealism, the ultimate subversion and sublimation of Kunztian Rationalism into Haggian Idealism.

Ultramaterialism believes that all the belief in a greater world, a platonic world of ideas, is true and that it is where all materiality comes from.

They believe that it goes as thus: ideas from the Universal DIA/ Platonic World -> Phenomenal Reality -> Ideas in the Personal DIA/ Singular Consciousness. They believe that through meditation, mind-sciences, dialectic, scholarly pursuit, and philosophical inquiry into the Phenomenal Reality, we can find a connection with the Universal DIA, and therefore influence the Universal DIA. The Law Cultivators-syncretists among Ultramaterialists understand that the world is us, and we are the world. That the Noumenal world is reachable and is, in fact, manipulable by the sheer Spirit of Consciousness, which itself can be harnessed and wielded as it arises from material conditions.

Truth · d66 [6][2]

Worship of the Darkness and the Void. An offshoot of Infinite Code after the teachings of the Earth Store and Heaven Womb were given to the 10 Disciples after the Sanja Kitama’s return from the 66 God Heaven.

Mostly espoused by the tenth Disciple Zanyata, who took Darkness to be synonymous with Emptiness, and that ultimate Nirvana is the reattainment of Blissful Sacred Dark.

Zanyatists worship the night, the dark, shadows, and all forms of gloam, creating blades, weaponry, and other gear from their most sacred materials: Nighstone and Duskmetal. They otherwise are part of the Law canon and Zanyatists are considered followers of the Law.

Truth · d66 [6][3]

The world is arranged according to the stars, and they should follow the Star Omens to create a perfect society. The great Lusbel, the brightest star, Deity of the Dawn.

His blood is Soma, food of the deities. Filled with powerful cultivating essence. Was once the Blacklight Star, who allowed passive Cultivation upon the entire world, but was split in two by Kanzen Immortal in his tyranny. Lusbel therefore became a Companion of the Law and a great enemy of the Yajists.

Truth · d66 [6][4]

The world is arranged according to the darkness between the stars, and one should follow the Void to create a society for cultivating loving individuals. The great Sunran, the brightest star, Deity of the Dusk. She is a Cultivator but also one who sees every interpenetrating strand of romantic and sexual love.

She is the God of Generation, her semen is Soma, food of wizards, and is filled with powerful cultivating essence. Was once the Blacklight Star, before split in two by the tyrant Kanzen Immortal. Sunran is cursed to never see her other half, and therefore wanders. Though not harnessed of the same hatred of Yajists, she almost never leaves her sidereal vehicle.

Truth · d66 [6][5]–[6][6]

The world must understand that it is not separate from the Greatest of All Existence. Only then can we break through dividing lines and embody love almighty. The Absolute Reality, divorced from phenomenal reality. The Scarlet God is the most popular deity in the Utter Islands. A pantheon of deities are said to be just manifestations or aspects of the Scarlet God. The Scarlet God Rutra himself was once the Screaming God, the Howling Wind. This God of Destruction embodied true creation, ripping away the trappings of mortal-made ritual and emphasizing devotion and esoteric practice. The main soteriological belief in Rutraism is that all things are just manifestations arising from the great Supreme Soul, that Soul being Rutra.

He is the Greatest God, the Highest of All Gods, the Ultimate Reality. Our goal is to break free from the mental fetters that keep us from seeing reality as-it-is, as a manifestation of Rutra. This is done through various rituals, devotions, and antinomian acts that rip apart the idea of reality-as-we-know-it to replace it with the greater, Ultimate Reality.

The state of finding Unity with the Supreme Soul is known as Puksa, a Selorongian word that now means both Annihilation and Liberation, as Annihilation of Ego to attain complete Unity with the Greatest Power is in itself an act of Liberation.
